_comment: Every dataset the build needs, and every way it can be obtained.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Not all connectors are live yet, and the ones that are can be
stale without saying so. Austin's requirement: build the whole thing now
against files we can refresh by hand, and when a connector comes online flip a
switch rather than rebuild. So each dataset declares an ordered list of
providers. sources.py walks them, takes the first that yields data, normalises
to the dataset's canonical fields and records which provider served it.
THE SWITCH is the `enabled` flag and the provider order. No code changes.
ONE LANDING ZONE. Neither the automated path nor the manual path talks to
SharePoint from Python -- the container has no credentials. The routine fetches
through the MCP connector and writes into pipeline/incoming/<dataset>/, and a
human dropping a file by hand writes to the same place. Identical downstream,
so the fallback cannot drift from the primary. See pipeline/manual/README.md.
AS-OF, ALWAYS. Every provider must yield an as_of date. The capture keys on it
rather than on the run date, so an unrefreshed source costs a day of history
instead of fabricating one. See docs/PLATFORM_SPEC.md.

providers.name: sharepoint_daily
providers._note: Primary. Lands ~08:05 ET, 387 files of history. 125 columns.

providers.name: rm_api
providers._note: Fallback. Only 30 columns -- no stage dates, no punch out. Do not promote above sharepoint_daily.

providers.name: manual
providers._note: Last resort. Same shape as sharepoint_daily; drop it in pipeline/manual/.

_stage_date_caveat: THE STAGE COLUMNS ARE FREE TEXT, NOT DATES. Checked 2026-09-06: of 1,745
assets only 96 carry any punch-out value at all, and of those 80 read 'TBD',
3 read 'N/A', 3 read 'WE 07/07/26' (a week-ending convention) and 9 are a
real date. Every stage column behaves the same way.
So the punch stage EXISTS in Rent Manager -- which corrects the dashboard note
saying it does not -- but the field is a hand-typed planning cell with mixed
conventions, not an event log. Durations cannot be computed from it today.
DERIVE DURATIONS FROM THE DAILY SNAPSHOTS INSTEAD. With 387 dated files we can
diff `status` across consecutive days and observe when a home actually moved
between stages. That measures what happened rather than trusting what someone
typed, and it needs no data-entry change to start working.
Keep reading these columns anyway: they are the team's forward-looking target
dates, which is a different and useful thing, and 'TBD' at 83% is itself a
finding worth putting in front of whoever owns home setup.

_comment: The actual completion date per home per setup stage, as stamped by the crew.
Coming from FastField forms into the Quickbase project, which is moving
slowly. Declared now and disabled so that when it lands it is a flag flip
rather than a rebuild.
Do NOT add actual-date fields to Rent Manager to fill the gap. The capture is
already designed in FastField; a parallel set in RM would create two answers
to the same question. Until this exists, durations are derived from Current
Status transitions across the daily snapshots -- coarser (five or six
milestones, not fifteen) but observed rather than typed.
